verdicts.note: Verified in rollcalls-6346/2081/5813/5814/5801.xml: yea on ESSB 6346 and ESHB 2081; nay on ESSB 5813, 5814 and 5801; yea on 33 of the 65 rejected 6346 floor amendments. That is genuinely split, so 0 medium.
Rests on the pamphlet and site investment language [S1][S3]. Appropriations membership in the basis is not directional evidence and should not carry weight.

Missed nuance in the cited roll calls [S18]: on 2025-04-23 she voted yea on concurring in the Senate amendments (failed 48-50). Those amendments set a looser cap: 10 percent plus CPI and a single-family exemption (Senate floor amendments 345 Shewmake and 312 Liias). So she voted against the 7 percent House version and the 7 percent + CPI/10 percent conference version, but for enacting the looser cap. That supports 0 more than it undercuts it. The dossier Record line should add the concur vote.

Checked rollcalls-1296.xml: besides yea on House third reading (2025-03-12) and final passage as amended by the Senate (2025-04-24), Leavitt voted nay on all ten contested Republican floor amendments roll-called on 2025-03-12 that would have added to the I-2081 rights list (e.g. Burnett 382, monthly evening/weekend curriculum review; 39-42 yeas each), and yea only on two near-unanimous ones (Couture 428, immediate notification of alleged staff sexual misconduct, 93-0; Barkis 462, right to request charter-school enrollment, 92-1). That is not a mixed record: every split vote went toward school discretion, and the two consensus yeas only argue against +2, which was not given. +1 high stands on recorded votes. The dossier should add the amendment votes under Parents and schools.
Repeated across the priorities page and two dated 2026 posts [S3][S5][S6], with State Auditor accountability findings. That meets the bar for high.
Concern about taxes and high-earner flight with no pledge [S5][S6][S9]. -1 medium is appropriately modest.

Read the cached post [S7]. She lists law enforcement accountability, first responders, treatment and prevention alongside 'safety and order', and says 'We cannot arrest our way out of every problem.' It does say 'state leadership has lost sight of balance' and names repeat offenders and open drug use, which leans slightly toward enforcement against the status quo, but the stated position is explicitly balanced. 0 medium holds.
